details: Whole Body Counting (WBC): measures in-vivo gamma activity from internally deposited radionuclides; Cs-137 (662 keV gamma via Ba-137m): detectable at 270 Bq threshold in standard scan (4π geometry NaI array; 5min count; 70 kg adult); Cs-134 (605/796 keV): similar threshold; I-131 (365 keV): WBC can detect but thyroid-specific detector more sensitive (see thyroid scanning); Sr-90: NOT detectable by WBC (pure beta emitter; no gamma); Pu-239: NOT detectable by WBC (alpha emitter; 17 keV X-ray too low energy; <1% escapes body); Co-60 (1173/1332 keV): detectable at ~100 Bq; Cs-137 effective half-life in body: 70d (adult); 30d (child <5yr); biological excretion rate ~1%/day
chernobyl_application: WBC in Chernobyl populations: Ukrainian Institute of Radiation Medicine performed 200,000+ WBC measurements 1991-2020 (Zhytomyr screening program); body burden decline: mean 21.6 Bq/kg (1991) → 3.0 Bq/kg (2018); autumn peaks from mushroom/forest berry consumption (seasonal Cs-137 intake spike); current self-settler body burdens: 10-100 Bq/kg Cs-137 (dietary exposure ongoing); children with same diet as adults get higher committed doses per kg (higher food intake/body mass ratio); see cs137_body_burden_ukraine_REAL.csv for longitudinal data
source: IAEA Safety Reports Series No. 14 (1998); Balonov 2007; cs137_body_burden_ukraine_REAL.csv; dose_conversion_factors_REAL.csv

details: Thyroid scanning for I-131: directional NaI(Tl) detector aimed at anterior neck; measures 364 keV gamma from I-131; sensitivity: ~10-100 Bq in thyroid (dedicated thyroid counter); threshold for reliable dose reconstruction: ~1000 Bq at time of measurement (above which uncertainty from position/geometry <30%); Soviet 1986 measurements: ~400,000 performed but mostly May-June 1986 (3-5 half-lives after peak exposure = 8-32x lower than peak value); conversion: measured Bq → peak activity (must know date of measurement relative to contamination event); from peak activity → thyroid dose using ICRP 30 thyroid model (dose coefficient 1.4×10⁻⁵ Gy/Bq for 10-week retention); adult thyroid mass = 20g; child = 5-10g (ratio 2-4x → child dose per Bq = 2-4x higher before even considering dose coefficient age factor)
chernobyl_application: Practical problem: Soviet thyroid measurements largely unusable for dose reconstruction because: (1) delay too long (I-131 decayed); (2) calibration variable; (3) records lost; (4) geometric correction not standardized; studies using these measurements (Likhtarev 1995; Gavrilin 1999) applied correction factors of 8-32× for measurement timing delay plus calibration corrections; resulting uncertainty: ×3-5 for individual estimates; alternative: use fallout deposition maps + food consumption surveys + ICRP models → comparable or better precision in aggregate; RADRUE methodology uses both approaches combined for thyroid dose component
source: Likhtarev 1995 Radiat Environ Biophys 34:143; Gavrilin 1999 Health Phys; unscear_evacuee_thyroid_doses_REAL.csv; iodine_atmospheric_chemistry_REAL.csv

details: ICRP 66 (1994) Human Respiratory Tract Model: defines lung clearance of inhaled particles; three absorption classes: F (Fast): soluble compounds; absorption half-time <10min; 100% absorbed to blood within hours; M (Moderate): typical insoluble compounds; half-time days-weeks; 10-15% rapid absorption + 90% slow clearance; S (Slow): insoluble refractory compounds; half-time months-years; minimal blood transfer; relevance to Chernobyl inhalation: I-131: class F (volatile; rapidly absorbed) → thyroid dose dominant; Cs-137 aerosol: class M-F (soluble CsOH/CsCl formed in plume) → absorbed to blood → whole-body distribution; Pu-239 fuel particles: class S or AMAD-dependent → pulmonary dose critical; fuel particles 4-150 µm → mostly deposit in upper airways; <5 µm particles reach alveoli
chernobyl_application: Chernobyl inhalation dose assessment: external gamma dominated inhalation dose for most distances/times; however inhalation critical for: (1) liquidators inside shelter (suspended dust; hot particles); (2) firefighters first night (smoke + steam); (3) populations near NW fuel particle deposition zone; AMAD (Activity Median Aerodynamic Diameter) for Cs-137 in Chernobyl plume: 0.3-3 µm (condensation aerosol); Pu particles (fuel): 4-150 µm → mostly nasal/bronchial deposition (class S behavior); dedicated lung dose models required for liquidator inhalation pathway; ICRP 130 (2015) updated lung model used for current worker protection

details: Ingestion dose pathways: (1) Milk pathway (cow → human): I-131 cow transfer factor Fm = 0.004 d/L (fraction of daily intake appearing in 1L milk on same day); sheep Fm = 0.29 d/L (70x cow); goat Fm = 0.14 d/L (35x cow); deposition to grass ingestion = same day; peak milk contamination: May 1-5 1986 in high-contamination areas; Belarus highest cow milk I-131: 5,000-1,000,000 Bq/L measured May 1986 (WHO guideline 500 Bq/L); (2) Beef pathway: slower (weeks after deposition peak); (3) Vegetables: leafy >root crops; (4) Grain: Cs-137 through soil-plant transfer; (5) Freshwater fish: Cs-137 primary (Sr-90 also); (6) Milk powder/processed: concentrated proportionally
chernobyl_application: Soviet milk ban timing: no ban until May 5-8 1986 in contaminated areas (10 days post-accident); significant adult and child I-131 intake during this window; Polish milk ban: April 29 1986 (3 days); explains partly why Belarus/Ukraine children had higher thyroid doses than Polish children; contaminated milk = single highest-dose exposure pathway for the pediatric thyroid cancer epidemic; Cs-137 in milk: peak 1986 then declining with soil-to-plant pathway dynamics; current (2026) Rivne/Zhytomyr milk: occasional exceedances in subsistence farming near CEZ outer zones (Cs-137 >> 100 Bq/L in goat milk from backyard animals fed local forage)
source: Ng 1990 Health Phys; soil_plant_transfer_factors_REAL.csv; food_agricultural_contamination_REAL.csv; ukraine_crop_contamination_REAL.csv; decontamination_countermeasures_REAL.csv

details: Committed effective dose E(50): integral over 50 years of effective dose rate from a single intake event; E(50) = Σ_T h_T × H_T(50) where h_T is tissue weighting factor and H_T(50) is committed equivalent dose to tissue T; ICRP 72 (1996) dose coefficients for ingestion: Cs-137 adult: 1.3×10⁻⁸ Sv/Bq; Cs-137 1yr child: 2.1×10⁻⁸ Sv/Bq (1.6x adult); I-131 adult thyroid contribution: 2.2×10⁻⁷ Sv/Bq (effective); I-131 1yr child: 1.8×10⁻⁶ Sv/Bq (8× adult!); Sr-90 adult: 2.8×10⁻⁸ Sv/Bq; Pu-239 ingestion adult: 2.5×10⁻⁷ Sv/Bq; Pu-239 inhalation adult (Type S): 3.2×10⁻⁵ Sv/Bq (1000× more than ingestion); Am-241 inhalation: 9.6×10⁻⁶ Sv/Bq
chernobyl_application: I-131 dose coefficient 8× higher for 1yr child vs adult: explains pediatric thyroid cancer excess; I-131 child dose = 8 (dose coefficient) × 3-4 (smaller thyroid mass per activity = higher tissue dose) × 1.5 (iodine deficiency amplification) = net 36-50× higher thyroid dose per unit activity intake for iodine-deficient child vs iodine-sufficient adult; this 36-50x factor explains why thyroid cancer is confined to childhood exposures (not adults); children exposed in utero had highest risk; dose coefficient age dependence = fundamental reason why pediatric exposure is the critical pathway

details: Prussian Blue (PB; ferric hexacyanoferrate; Fe₄[Fe(CN)₆]₃) for Cs-137 internal decorporation: mechanism: PB is insoluble cation exchanger; in gut lumen: Cs⁺ and Rb⁺ bind tightly to PB cage structure; interrupts enterohepatic recirculation of Cs-137 (normally ~5-10% of body burden/day excreted in bile → reabsorbed in gut); effective dose reduction: PB 3g/day → reduces biological half-life from 70d to 30-35d (adult); factor 2× reduction in committed dose; dose in Belarus self-settlers: 3g/day × 30 days prescribed after WBC screening > 1000 Bq/kg; licensed pharmaceutical: Radiogardase (HEYL Berlin); not an antidote (does not remove existing body burden rapidly) but interrupts recycling
chernobyl_application: CEZ self-settlers treated with Prussian Blue when WBC shows elevated Cs-137: 1990s-2000s: prescribing reduced as body burdens declined with dietary change; IAEA/WHO guidelines: prescribe when body burden >3 kBq (adult); child threshold lower; practical problem in CEZ: self-settlers unwilling to change diet (mushroom/berry consumption = cultural/nutritional importance); PB provides option to eat local food with reduced dose consequence; animal studies: PB in feed reduces Cs-137 in cattle meat/milk 30-50%; used in livestock management; not effective for Sr-90 (Sr chemical behavior different from Cs) or Pu (not absorbed from gut)
source: Stather 1989 Health Phys; Carr 1997 Health Phys; cs137_body_burden_ukraine_REAL.csv; decontamination_countermeasures_REAL.csv

details: Cs-137 biokinetic model: ICRP 30/67 model: after absorption from gut to blood (rapid for soluble Cs compounds); distribution: whole body (Cs = K analog); compartments: (1) Short biological half-life: t_b1 = 2 days (10% of activity; extracellular fluid); (2) Long biological half-life: t_b2 = 110 days (90% of activity; intracellular); effective half-life in body (combining radioactive t½ = 30.17yr with biological): t_eff = 1/(1/t_r + 1/t_b) ≈ t_b ≈ 70d (adult; biological dominates since 30yr >> 70d); child (1yr): t_b2 = 22 days → t_eff = 20 days; muscle = primary depot (analog to K⁺ → pumped into muscle cells by Na/K-ATPase); whole-body WBC measures total body inventory
chernobyl_application: Practical implication: Cs-137 body burden reflects dietary intake in preceding ~200 days (3 half-lives); autumn WBC peaks = mushroom consumption 2-6 weeks prior; WBC in spring: reflects previous year's low background + winter dietary Cs; biological half-life much shorter in children (20 days) = children clear Cs-137 faster but also accumulate faster per Bq intake/d relative to mass; RNMDR monitoring: annual WBC of liquidators; declining body burdens track declining environmental contamination; self-settlers: body burden provides objective dietary exposure assessment better than food frequency questionnaires
source: ICRP 30 1979; ICRP 67 1993; Balonov 1993 J Radiol Prot; cs137_body_burden_ukraine_REAL.csv

details: Sr-90 biokinetics: ICRP 20 (1973)/ICRP 67 (1993) model: Sr = Ca analog; pathway after ingestion: gut absorption fraction = 0.3 (adult); age-dependent: infant 0.6 (2× adult); bone as primary depot: trabecular and cortical bone surface initially; remodeling transfers Sr-90 to bone mineral volume; effective biological half-life in bone: ~50 years (bone mineral turnover rate); effective whole-body half-life: ~50yr (bone-seeking = long-lived internal contaminant); in blood: eliminated with t_b = 2 days for soft tissue fraction; committed bone marrow dose from Sr-90: important because bone marrow is alpha-critical tissue from Ra-226/Ra-228 but for Sr-90 beta dose to bone marrow and bone surface cells
chernobyl_application: Sr-90 internal dose in Chernobyl populations: Techa River Cohort (Mayak) provides best analogy for bone marrow Sr-90 doses; Techa mean marrow dose 0.5-4 Gy = leukemia risk confirmed; Chernobyl Sr-90 ingestion: much lower doses (thyroid doses from I-131 dominated internal dose in 1986; Sr-90 ingestion doses ~ 0.1-1 mSv/yr effective for contaminated food areas); Sr-90 in food chain: milk secondary to I-131 in 1986; grain residual pathway now (2026); Sr-90 in bone: CANNOT be measured by WBC (pure beta) → urine bioassay required (Sr excretion fraction 0.5-1%/day of absorbed dose); EPR can detect Sr-90 bone dose retrospectively (both Sr-90 beta and Ra-226 alpha cause EPR signal in enamel)
source: ICRP 67 1993; Kossenko 1997; Techa River Cohort data; stochastic_deterministic_effects_REAL.csv; ukraine_crop_contamination_REAL.csv
